 *FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL*
 3.

Facts leading to the case of the petitioners forthcoming in the petition averments that, on the fateful date of the alleged accident, on 9.11.2019 at about 5.30 p.m., Narasimhappa was riding his TVS XL Super Heavy duty bearing registratin No.KA-50- Q-4071, near Maraganahalli NH-7 road,
Chickaballapura Taluk, at that point of time, the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA-40- A-6689 drove the same in arash and negligent manner and dashed against the TVS XL.
Due to the said impact, Narasimhappa fell down and succumbed to the injuries at the spot.

5. It is alleged in the petitions that, the accident had taken place, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA-40-A-6689.

Hence, the petitioners have filed the respective petitions claiming compensation in the case on hand.
6. After registration of the case, as usual notices were issued to the respondents.

The respondent No.1 in MVC 141/2022 remained  6 SCCH-18 MVC 342/2020 & 141/2022 absent, placed exparte.
On the other hand respondent No.2 in both the cases filed the written statements in answer to the case of the petitioners.

in the accident.

Further contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased and not on the part of the driver of the Lorry.
And contended that the driver of the said Tipper Lorry had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle, at the time of  7 SCCH-18 MVC 342/2020 & 141/2022 accident.

26 . The petitioners herein, to prove the actual age of the deceased, as on the date of the accident,
petitioners have produced Aadhar card marked at Ex.P32, for consideration.
On going through Aadhar card marked at Ex.P32, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 1.1.1961.
The accident occurred on 9.11.2019.
If the said document is taken into consideration, as on the date of the accident, deceased Narasimhappa, was aged about 58 years.
And the said document, remained unquestioned by the other side.
Hence, I am of the view that, as on the date of the accident deceased was aged about 58 years.
For his age, multiplier '9' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.

In connection with the work of the deceased is concerned, in the main petition the PW1 has stated that, deceased Narasimhappa during his lifetime, was running dry cleaner shop and used to earn Rs.25,000/- per month.

In support of this, there is no iota of documents to show his definite income per Venkatamma vs Kesar Aggregates on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145365536/

In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income has to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
And also, it is apt to rely on the chart prepared by the legal services authority, with respect to the notional income.

Hence, by keeping in mind about the year of the institution of this case, I am of the view that, in the light of all the facts and circumstances of the present case, fully discussed above, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.14,000/- for the year 2019, which will meet the ends of justice.

An addition of 25 per  cent where the deceased was between the age of 40  to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the  deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years  and 10 per cent where the deceased was between  the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the  necessary method of computation.

In the light of the above  27 SCCH-18 MVC 342/2020 & 141/2022 proposition, in the case on hand, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
